feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Each invocation of the OP_CODESEPARATOR and OP_CHECKSIG pair necessitates generating a new scriptCode as outlined in BIP 143, which results in the computation of a fresh transaction digest for each call. This repeated recomputation is resource-intensive and was identified as a significant reason for proposals to deprecate OP_CODESEPARATOR in subsequent versions of Bitcoin Script.
Despite these concerns, the proliferation of SIGHASH flag combinations and existing SigOp constraints may mitigate the impact of this computational overhead. The cost associated with recomputing scriptCode when using OP_CODESEPARATOR might not be as substantial given the current limitations already imposed on signature operations within scripts.
Furthermore, even if the behavior of OP_CODESEPARATOR is eliminated in future iterations of Script, the need for its functionality can be alleviated by employing MAST (Merkelized Abstract Syntax Trees). With MAST, up to thirty sequential layers of OP_IF statements can be efficiently handled without resorting to OP_CODESEPARATOR, thus simplifying script complexity while maintaining robust conditional logic.
